meta.title: Directive 2013/48/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 22 October 2013 on the right of access to a lawyer in criminal proceedings and in European arrest warrant proceedings, and on the right to have a third party informed upon deprivation of liberty and to communicate with third persons and with consular authorities while deprived of liberty

items.text: This Directive lays down minimum rules concerning the rights of suspects and accused persons in criminal proceedings and of persons subject to proceedings pursuant to Framework Decision 2002/584/JHA (‘European arrest warrant proceedings’) to have access to a lawyer, to have a third party informed of the deprivation of liberty and to communicate with third persons and with consular authorities while deprived of liberty.
items.heading: Article 1
items.comment: No specific legal instrument was enacted in Portugal for the implementation of this Directive. Existing legislation was deemed to cover it. In our view, all the norms of the Directive have not sufficient backing in the legislation in force. Moreover, in our view, this is one of the Directives where implementation levels are poorer, and there is a clear need for legislative intervention here.

items.heading: Article 2

items.text: 1. This Directive applies to suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings from the time when they are made aware by the competent authorities of a Member State, by official notification or otherwise, that they are suspected or accused of having committed a criminal offence, and irrespective of whether they are deprived of liberty. It applies until the conclusion of the proceedings, which is understood to mean the final determination of the question whether the suspect or accused person has committed the offence, including, where applicable, sentencing and the resolution of any appeal.

nationalActs.title: Constituição da República Portuguesa (Decreto de 10 de Abril de 1976)
nationalActs.titleEn: Constitution of the Portuguese Republic (Decree of 10 April 1976)

provisions.textEn: Criminal procedure ensures all guarantees of defence, including the right to appeal.

Accused persons have the right to choose an attorney and to be assisted by him/her in any procedural act. The law shall specify the cases and phases of procedure in which the assistance of a lawyer is mandatory.
Subject to the terms of the law, everyone has the right to legal information and advice, to legal counsel and to be accompanied by a lawyer before any authority.

nationalActs.title: Código de Processo Penal (Decreto-Lei n.º 78/87, de 17 de Fevereiro)
nationalActs.titleEn: Code of Criminal Procedure (Decree-Law no. 78/87, of 17 February)

provisions.comment:
Articles 254 to 261 CCP, mentioned above, regulate the conditions in which a person may be arrested. Arrest (or detention) is different from pre-trial custodial detention, as outlined shortly below. It should be noted that, under Portuguese law, arrest and pre-trial custodial detention may not to be regarded as investigative measures, as they are not aimed at collecting evidence. Arrest is conceived of as a “cautionary measure” (medida cautelar) and custodial detention as a “coercive measure” (medida de coacção), and they serve different purposes:


a) Arrest is regulated mainly in Articles 254 f., according to which a person can be arrested in order to be tried within a maximum term of 48 hours under a special (more expeditious) form of proceedings called “summary proceedings” (processo sumário), or to have a coercive measure applied to him/her. It is also possible to arrest a person in order to take him/her immediately – or, if this is not possible, within a maximum term of 24 hours – to a judicial authority for attending a procedural act. When a person has been arrested in order to be tried under summary proceedings but this turned out not to be possible, or to be subjected to a coercive measure, this person must be interrogated by a judge within a maximum term of 48 hours (first judicial interrogation). Arrest in flagrante delicto is possible only for offences punishable with imprisonment (which applies, a fortiori, to the arrest of a person who has not been caught in flagrante delicto). Arrest without flagrante delicto may only take place based on an order of a judge or, if pre-trial custodial detention is admissible in the case, by the Public Prosecution, provided that there is good reason to believe that the person would not present him/herself spontaneously before a judicial authority within the due term. In case of urgency, even if there is no flagrante delicto, the police may arrest a person, but this arrest must be communicated either to a judge or to the Public Prosecution (depending on its purpose) for validation. The defendant may appeal these decisions, and habeas corpus against unlawful detention may be invoked by any citizen in the exercise of his/her political rights. It is also possible to arrest a person if his/her extradition has been requested and a judge finds the request to be prima facie viable. Finally, a person may also be arrested if a EAW has been duly issued, although this type of arrest must still comply with the provisions of the CCP on arrest, outlined above. 


b) Pre-trial custodial detention can only be applied if there is “strong evidence” (fortes indícios) that the defendant has intentionally committed an offence punishable with imprisonment for over 5 years, or for over 3 years in some cases. This measure can also be applied, regardless of a specific degree of suspicion and of the offence in question, if the person is requested for extradition. As for the EAW, the CCP does not explicitly establish that receiving one such request enables the authorities to apply this measure, but the Supreme Court has ruled that the EAW, as a swifter form of extradition, abides by the same rules as classic extradition insofar as this issue is concerned. As all other coercive measures regulated in the CCP, pre-trial custodial detention may only be applied if: (i) the defendant has escaped or there is a risk that he/she will escape; (ii) there is a risk that he/she will disturb the investigation, notably the gathering of evidence or its veracity, by destroying or tampering with it; or (iii) there is a risk that the defendant will continue his/her criminal activity or cause severe public upheaval. On the other hand, custodial detention – as well as house arrest (obrigação de permanência na habitação) – can only be applied where other coercive measures which do not involve deprivation of liberty show inadequate or ineffective. This measure can only be ordered by a judge, after hearing the defendant in the mandatory presence of his/her lawyer, except for cases of justified impossibility, and it may not be based upon facts or elements which are not provided or communicated to the defendant during that hearing. 


This measure is subject to maximum terms which are established in the CPP (Article 215), and that the decision to apply this measure (or to maintain it, if it had already been applied) can be appealed against, an appeal which must be ruled on within a maximum term of 30 days. Again, any citizen in the exercise of his/her political rights may file a habeas corpus request against illegal imprisonment as a means to react against the application of pre-trial custodial detention.
provisions.textEn:
(1) Without detriment to Article 57, the designation as defendant (arguido) is also mandatory as soon as:

(a) A person makes statements before any judicial authority or criminal police body during an inquiry initiated against him/her, where there are grounds to suspect that such person has committed a criminal offence;

(b) A coercive or patrimonial guarantee measure must be imposed on him/her;

(c) A suspect is arrested under the terms and for the purposes of Articles 254 to 261 of this Code; or

(d) A police report has been drawn up identifying a person as an alleged offender and that person has been informed on the contents thereof, unless the report is clearly unfounded.

(2) The status of defendant is acquired with the communication to the concerned person, either orally or in writing, by a judicial authority or criminal police body that, as of that moment, he/she has the status of defendant in criminal proceedings and, if necessary, by the explanation of procedural rights and duties of defendants laid down in Article 61, which he/she is thenceforth bound to observe.

(3) If the act is carried out by the criminal police, it must be communicated to a judicial authority within 10 days, so that this authority may, within another 10-day term, examine and decide whether or not the act is to be considered valid.

(4) The status of arguido implies the delivery to the concerned person, if possible simultaneously, of a document specifying details on the case and on the defence attorney, if one has already been appointed, and such a document must also indicate the rights and duties that the person is thenceforth entitled to.

(5) Failure to comply with the formalities laid down in this Article carry a prohibition to use as evidence any statements made by the concerned person.

(6) The non-validation of the act designating a person as arguido by the judicial authority does not affect the evidence that has been previously collected.

(1) If a founded suspicion emerges during the course of an interrogation of a person who is not a defendant has committed an offence, the authority performing such an interrogation shall suspend it immediately and effect the communication and the advice mentioned in Article 58 (2) CCP.

(2) A person suspected of having committed an offence has the right to be designated as a defendant at his/her own request, whenever an investigation is being carried out with a view to establishing his/her criminal liability and measures are being taken which personally affect him/her.

(3) The provisions of Article 58 (3) and (4) apply accordingly.

As of the moment when a person is assigned the status of defendant (arguido), he/she is entitled to exercise procedural rights and duties, without detriment to the application of coercive measures and measures of patrimonial guarantee, as well as the carrying out of evidentiary measures in the legally prescribed terms.

Unless otherwise provided for in the law, the defendant is specifically entitled, at all stages of the procedure, to the following rights: (…) to appoint a lawyer or request that one be appointed to him/her.

Unless otherwise provided for in the law, the defendant is specifically entitled, at all stages of the procedure, to the following rights: (…) to be assisted by a defence lawyer in every procedural act in which he/she takes part, and, if arrested, to communicate with him/her in private.

items.text: 2. This Directive applies to persons subject to European arrest warrant proceedings (requested persons) from the time of their arrest in the executing Member State in accordance with Article 10.

provisions.textEn: A person arrested pursuant to an EAW has the right to be assisted by an attorney.

provisions.comment: LEAW further explicitly requires the assistance of an attorney in other procedural acts, such as that where the sought person consents to waiving the specialty rule (see Article 7 (3) (c)), to being re-surrendered to a different Member State following the execution of an EAW (see Article 8 (2) (c)), or to being surrendered to the issuing Member State (see Article 21).
provisions.textEn: [When a person who has been arrested pursuant to an EAW request, this person should be brought before a judge within 48 hours and, before hearing the person,] The judge in charge of the case shall appoint him/her an attorney, in case he/she has not yet appointed one by his/her own initiative.

items.text: 3. This Directive also applies, under the same conditions as provided for in paragraph 1, to persons other than suspects or accused persons who, in the course of questioning by the police or by another law enforcement authority, become suspects or accused persons.

nationalActs.titleEn: Law on Penal Mediation

provisions.comment:
Penal Mediation:

During the phase of inquiry, the public prosecutor in charge of the case may decide, either by his/her own initiative or at request of the defendant or the victim, and provided that both of them so agree, that the case be submitted to penal mediation (mediação penal). This possibility has been introduced into the Portuguese procedural system by the mentioned Law no 21/2007 of 12 June.

Penal mediation is possible both for public and private offences lato sensu (private offences lato sensu are offences that can only be investigated and/or prosecuted if the victim so wishes), but insofar as concerns semi-public offences (i.e., offences that can only be prosecuted if the victim so wishes) this is only possible in the specific case of offences against the individual or against property).

Regardless of whether the offence is a public or private offence, this mediation regime cannot be resorted to if: (a) the crime is punishable with imprisonment exceeding five years; (b) the object of the procedure is a sex crime, a crime of peculation, corruption or influence peddling; (c) the victim is a minor under 16 years old; or (d) the special forms of proceedings of processo sumário or processo sumaríssimo are applicable.

The public prosecution service may decide that the case be submitted to penal mediation at any time of the procedure, but only after and if it has gathered sufficient evidence that the crime was indeed committed by the defendant, and if it believes that penal mediation is adequate to fulfilling the purposes of punishment (that is, deterrence: see Article 40 (1) of the Penal Code). However, these conditions do not apply if the submission of the case to penal mediation is requested by the defendant or the victim themselves and both agree to this course of action.
provisions.textEn: The defendant and the victim must attend the mediation session in person, and they may be accompanied by an attorney or an intern attorney.

items.comment: Apart from the possibility of penal mediation, even minor penalties must be applied by a court endowed with jurisdiction in criminal matters; and the regime of penal mediation still confers on the defendant the right to be assisted by an attorney at all stages of the proceedings.

items.heading: Article 3
items.subHeading: The right of access to a lawyer in criminal proceedings
items.comment: See the provisions immediately above, especially, Articles 58 (1) (c) and 61 (1) (f) of the CCP.

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that suspects and accused persons have the right of access to a lawyer in such time and in such a manner so as to allow the persons concerned to exercise their rights of defence practically and effectively.
items.comment: Please refer to the provisions and comments attached to Article 2 of this Directive.

items.text: 2. Suspects or accused persons shall have access to a lawyer without undue delay. In any event, suspects or accused persons shall have access to a lawyer from whichever of the following points in time is the earliest:

nationalActs.title: Código de Processo Penal (Decreto-Lei n.º 78/87, de 17 de Fevereiro)
nationalActs.titleEn: Code of Criminal Procedure (Decree-Law no. 78/87, of 17 February)

provisions.comment: Articles 271 and 294 CCP refer to the so-called ‘taking of statements for future memory’ (declarações para memória futura): when it is probable that a witness cannot be present in trial, owing for instance to an illness, the judge may question this person (as well as victims of human trafficking and of sexual offences) before the trial, under specific conditions, with the exceptional possibility of using their declarations as direct evidence later in the trial – and, thus, in deviation from the principles of orality and immediacy. In those cases, the presence of the lawyer of the defendant is essential, because that procedural act is the crucial moment for exerting the right to contradict the testimony (audi alteram partem).
provisions.textEn:
(1) Assistance by an attorney is mandatory:

(a) In interrogations of an arrested or imprisoned defendant;

(b) In interrogations conducted by judicial authorities [a judge or a public prosecutor];

(c) In the debate that takes place at the end of the phase of instruction and in the trial hearing;

(d) In any procedural act, save for the formal designation of the person as a defendant, whenever the person is blind, deaf, speechless, illiterate, unfamiliar with the Portuguese language, a person under 21 years old, or the question has been raised whether he/she may lack criminal liability [owing to a mental disorder] or is not completely imputable;

(e) In any appeal, ordinary as well as extraordinary;

(f) In the cases mentioned in Articles 271 and 294;

(g) At the trial hearing held in the absence of the defendant;

(h) In any other case provided for by the law.

(2) Apart from the cases mentioned in the previous paragraph, the defendant may be appointed a lawyer, either at the request of the court or the defendant him/herself, whenever the circumstances of the case reveal a need for or convenience in having the defendant be assisted by a lawyer.

(3) Without detriment to the previous paragraphs, if the defendant does not yet have a lawyer, he/she must be appointed one when he/she is prosecuted, and this lawyer must be indicated in the order that puts an end to the phase of inquiry.

(4) In the case mentioned in the previous paragraph, the defendant is informed, in the bill of prosecution, that, should he/she be convicted, he/she will be obliged to pay for the services of the lawyer that has been appointed to him/her, unless he/she is granted legal aid, and that he/she may substitute such a lawyer by another lawyer of his/her choice.

items.comment: As follows from the provisions and comments attached to Article 2 of this Directive and from the provisions immediately below is that Portuguese law entitles defendants to a right of access to a lawyer in all cases listed in Article 3 (2) of the Directive, and that in many of these cases assistance by a lawyer is mandatory. However, not all the cases listed in Article 3 (2) of the Directive are cases in which Portuguese law imposes the assistance of a lawyer, and Article 3 (2) of the Directive (in contrast with its Article 3 (1)) may plausibly be interpreted as requiring the defendant, not simply to be given a right of access to a lawyer, but to be actively provided “access to a lawyer” by the State. If Article 3 (2) of the Directive is to be construed as establishing a mere right to lawyer, then Portuguese law is fully compliant; if, on the contrary, Article 3 (2) of the Directive establishes cases of mandatory assistance by a lawyer, then only some cases (notably those covered by Article 64 CPP) respond to the command of the Directive. The comments below assume that the latter is the proper interpretation.

provisions.textEn: Assistance by an attorney is mandatory: (...) In interrogations conducted by judicial authorities [a judge or a public prosecutor];

items.comment:
Only partially implemented.

Item (a) would be implemented only regarding interrogations performed by judicial authorities, but not by the police (see again Article 64 (1) (b) CCP). In any event, it should be noted that one of the reasons why Portuguese procedural law does not require the presence of a lawyer in interrogations before the police is that such statements may virtually never serve as evidence later in trial (see again Article 357 (1) (b) CCP). In fact, the Directive requiring the mandatory presence of a lawyer in interrogations carried out by the police could be regarded by the Portuguese legislator as an invitation to admit those statements as evidence. This would ironically represent a compression of fundamental rights, whereas the aim of the Directive is obviously the opposite.

provisions.comment: However, this provision does not in fact require the presence of the lawyer. Moreover, it is conceived as a cautionary or police measure and is, therefore, not an actual investigative measure aimed at obtaining evidence to be used later in trial. Actual identity parades (reconhecimentos de pessoas) are instead regulated in Articles 147 f. CCP, which do not even mention the possibility to contact a person of his/her trust – although, as noted repeatedly, a person does have the right to be assisted by a lawyer if he/she has been formally designated as a defendant, and a person regarding which investigation measures are being conducted always has the right to request his/her designation as a defendant if authorities do not do so ex officio. The same applies to confrontations (acareações), regulated in Article 146 CCP, and to reconstructions of the scene of a crime (reconstituições do facto), regulated in Article 150 CCP.
provisions.textEn: [If the criminal police is to proceed to the identification of a person who is suspected of having committed a crime,] The the person is always given the possibility to contact a person of his/her trust.

items.comment:
Only partially implemented.

Item (b) too could be deemed to be only partially implemented. The key national provision here is Article 250 (9) CPP, according to which, if the criminal police is to proceed to the identification of a suspect, this person is always given the possibility to contact a person of his/her trust. However, this provision does not in fact require the presence of the lawyer. Moreover, it is conceived as a cautionary or police measure and is, therefore, not an actual investigative measure aimed at obtaining evidence to be used later in trial. Actual identity parades (reconhecimentos de pessoas) are instead regulated in Articles 147 f. CCP, which do not even mention the possibility to contact a person of his/her trust – although, as noted repeatedly, a person does have the right to be assisted by a lawyer if he/she has been formally designated as a defendant, and a person regarding which investigation measures are being conducted always has the right to request his/her designation as a defendant if authorities do not do so ex officio. The same applies to confrontations (acareações), regulated in Article 146 CCP, and to reconstructions of the scene of a crime (reconstituições do facto), regulated in Article 150 CCP.

provisions.comment: In consequence of this provision, the array of rights conferred on the defendant, described above, may be exercised by his/her attorney. Still, on specific occasions the law further confirms that the lawyer has the right to participate effectively in the procedure, as is the case, v.g., with the provisions indicated immediately below.
provisions.textEn:
(1) The lawyer exercises all the rights that the law confers upon the defendant, save for those that are personally reserved to the latter.

(2) The defendant may revoke the act performed by his/her attorney on his/her behalf, so long as this is made by an explicit statement prior to the decision to be taken with respect to such an act.

(1) The phase of instruction [as noted already, this is a judicial phase which may take place following the inquiry and prior to the trial, with a view to ascertaining whether the defendant should be brought to trial] is composed of all the investigative acts that the judge deems necessary to be carried out and, mandatorily, by an oral debate in which may participate the public prosecution, the defendant and his/her lawyer, and the victim and his/her lawyer (...).

(2) The public prosecution, the defendant and his/her lawyer, and the victim and his/her lawyer may attend any investigative act requested by any of them during this phase, as well as request any clarification or the formulation of any questions that they deem relevant for ascertaining the truth of the facts.

[In the debate mentioned in Article 289] The judge ensures that the parties may contradict each other regarding the production of evidence and that the defendant or his/her lawyer are the last ones to speak.

(...)

(2) Afterwards the judge gives the floor to the public prosecution, to the lawyer of the victim and to the lawyer of the defendant, so that they may, if they so wish, request the production of further evidence (...).

(4) Before closing the debate, the judge gives again the floor to the public prosecution, to the lawyer of the victim and to the lawyer of the defendant, so that they may, if they so wish, formulate their summary conclusions as to the whether or not [the defendant should be indicted].

(5) Each of these subjects may replicate the intervention of other subjects in a summary manner and only once, but the lawyer of the defendant, if he/she wishes to speak, is always the last one to do so.

[At the trial hearing] Subsequently, the presiding judge gives the floor, in the following order, to the public prosecution, (...) and the lawyer of the defendant, so that they may, if they so wish, indicate, in a summary manner and in no longer than 10 minutes, the facts that they propose to prove.

[When questioning the defendant at the trial hearing] The public prosecution, the lawyer of the defendant [et al.] may not interfere with the statements of the defendant (...), save for the case provided for in Article 345 (1).

If the defendant is willing to make statements, each judge and juror may ask him/her questions (...). The defendant may, either spontaneously or upon recommendation of his/her lawyer, refuse to answer the question or all of the questions, and this may not be detrimental to the defendant.

(1) [At the end of the trial hearing,] After the production of evidence, the judge gives the floor to the public prosecution, (...) and the lawyer of the defendant, so that they may adduce oral allegations in which they present the conclusions, on factual as well as legal issues, that they have drawn from the produced evidence.

(2) Each subject may replicate the allegations of the others, once only, but the lawyer of the defendant, if he/she wishes to speak, is always the last to do so, or otherwise the hearing will be null (...).

provisions.comment: Article 169 CCP provides that the facts reported in an authentic or authenticated document are considered proven insofar as the veracity of the document or of the information contained therein is not justifiably brought into question.
provisions.textEn:
(1) The procedural acts that the law requires to be recorded, as well as statements, requests, promotions and decisions orally uttered, must be recorded in a written document called ‘auto’ [hereinafter ‘official record’].

(...)

(3) An official record contains, in addition to those required for written acts, the following elements:

(a) The identification of the persons who took part in the procedural act;

(...)

(c) A detailed description of the operations carried out, of the intervention of each procedural participant, of the statements made, and of the manner and circumstances in which they were made, including the indication of the beginning and end of each statement, when an audio or audiovisual recording is to be made, of the documents that have been presented or received and of the results obtained, so as to guarantee a genuine record of the procedural act;

(d) Any occurrence which shows relevant for assessing the evidence or the lawfulness of the procedural act.

(4) Article 169 applies accordingly.

provisions.comment: See also Article 275, concerning the phase of inquiry, and Articles 296 and 305, concerning the phase of instruction.
provisions.textEn: The statements made orally at the trial hearing are always recorded in the official record, or otherwise the hearing is null.
The procedural acts which are to be practiced in writing must be drafted in a perfectly intelligible manner (...).

items.text:
(c)

Member States shall ensure that suspects or accused persons shall have, as a minimum, the right for their lawyer to attend the following investigative or evidence-gathering acts where those acts are provided for under national law and if the suspect or accused person is required or permitted to attend the act concerned:
items.comment: As noted earlier, the defendant always has the right to have his/her lawyer present at these investigating or evidence-gathering acts, although this presence is not mandatory. But unlike the provisions above, Article 3 (3) (c) ‘only’ requires that the defendants be ensured a ‘right’ for their lawyer to attend these acts, such that, in this case, Portuguese law should be considered as fully compliant with the Directive.

identity parades;

items.text: 4. Member States shall endeavour to make general information available to facilitate the obtaining of a lawyer by suspects or accused persons.
items.comment: Considering the provisions mentioned throughout this transposition assessment, it seems safe to conclude that Portuguese law complies with this provision, in that it makes sufficiently available general information to facilitate the obtaining of a lawyer by suspects or accused persons, as well as to ensure that suspects or accused persons who are deprived of liberty are in a position to exercise effectively their right of access to a lawyer. Moreover, in the case where the presence of a lawyer in a given procedural act is mandatory (notably in the cases mentioned in Article 64 of the CCP, above), the defendant is not even entitled to waive this presence. Do however see the comments on the issue of the waiver by the defendant, regulated in Article 9 of this Directive.

items.text: Notwithstanding provisions of national law concerning the mandatory presence of a lawyer, Member States shall make the necessary arrangements to ensure that suspects or accused persons who are deprived of liberty are in a position to exercise effectively their right of access to a lawyer, unless they have waived that right in accordance with Article 9.
items.comment: Idem.

items.text: 5. In exceptional circumstances and only at the pre-trial stage, Member States may temporarily derogate from the application of point (c) of paragraph 2 where the geographical remoteness of a suspect or accused person makes it impossible to ensure the right of access to a lawyer without undue delay after deprivation of liberty.
items.comment: No such exceptions are admitted in the Portuguese legal system, such that these provisions of the Directive should be considered as fully implemented.

items.text: 6. In exceptional circumstances and only at the pre-trial stage, Member States may temporarily derogate from the application of the rights provided for in paragraph 3 to the extent justified in the light of the particular circumstances of the case, on the basis of one of the following compelling reasons:
items.comment: Idem.

items.text:
(a)

where there is an urgent need to avert serious adverse consequences for the life, liberty or physical integrity of a person;
items.comment: Idem.

items.text:
(b)

where immediate action by the investigating authorities is imperative to prevent substantial jeopardy to criminal proceedings.
items.comment: Idem.

items.text: Member States shall respect the confidentiality of communication between suspects or accused persons and their lawyer in the exercise of the right of access to a lawyer provided for under this Directive. Such communication shall include meetings, correspondence, telephone conversations and other forms of communication permitted under national law.
items.heading: Article 4

nationalActs.title: Constituição da República Portuguesa (Decreto de 10 de Abril de 1976)
nationalActs.titleEn: Constitution of the Portuguese Republic (Decree of 10 April 1976)

provisions.textEn: Accused persons have the right to choose an attorney and to be assisted by him/her in any procedural act. The law shall specify the cases and phases of procedure in which the assistance of a lawyer is mandatory.
Subject to the terms of the law, everyone has the right to legal information and advice, to legal counsel and to be accompanied by a lawyer before any authority.
All evidence obtained with torture, coercion, violation of physical or moral integrity, or improper intromission into personal life, the home, correspondence or telecommunications is null and void.

(1) Domiciles and the secrecy of correspondence and other means of private communication are inviolable.

(2) Entry into the domicile of a citizen against his/her will may only be ordered by the competent judicial authority and only in the cases and in compliance with the terms provided for by law.

(3) No one may enter the domicile of a person during the night without his/her consent, save in situations of flagrante delicto, or with judicial authorisation in cases of especially violent or highly organised crime including terrorism and trafficking in persons, arms or narcotics, as laid down by law.

(4) Public authorities cannot interfere in any way with correspondence, telecommunications or other means of communication, save in the cases in which the law so provides in matters related to criminal procedure.

nationalActs.title: Código de Processo Penal (Decreto-Lei n.º 78/87, de 17 de Fevereiro)
nationalActs.titleEn: Code of Criminal Procedure (Decree-Law no. 78/87, of 17 February)

provisions.textEn: Unless otherwise provided for in the law, the defendant is specifically entitled, at all stages of the procedure, to the following rights: (…) to be assisted by a defence lawyer in every procedural act in which he/she takes part, and, if arrested, to communicate with him/her in private.

The communication mentioned in paragraph (1) (f) takes place in plain sight when this is necessary for security reasons. However, conditions must be provision so that the person in charge of overseeing the communication does not hear it.

provisions.comment: Do however note that – differently than evidence obtained through torture, coercion or harm to physical or moral integrity (regulated in Article 126 (1) and (2) CCP) –, evidence gathered through intrusion in private life, domicile, mail or telecommunications may be consented to by the concerned person, either ex ante or ex post facto, and if so the nullity will be cured. Moreover, whereas the nullity established by Articles 126 (1) and (2) bears no exceptions, Article 126 (3) excepts the cases “where the law provides otherwise”, which refers to the intrusive investigative measures allowed for and regulated in the CCP (in Articles 171 f.) and in other special legal instruments of criminal procedure.
provisions.textEn: To the exception of the cases where the law provides otherwise, evidence obtained through intrusion, without the consent of the person concerned, in his/her private life, domicile, mail or telecommunications is also null.

provisions.comment: This applies to the cases regulated in paragraphs (1) and (2) as well as to those regulated in paragraph (3).
provisions.textEn: If the use of the evidence-gathering methods mentioned in this Articles constitutes a crime, such evidence may be used for the exclusive purpose of prosecuting those who used such methods.

provisions.comment:
In this case, however, the execution of the measure is restricted to that specific offence (v.g. receiving stolen goods), and not to the offence that was being investigated (v.g. the theft whence the stolen goods proceed).

Due to Article 189 of the CCP, Article 187 (5) applies to all forms of communication (telephone, e-mail and other forms of telematic transmission of data).
provisions.textEn: The interception and recording of conversations or communications between the defendant and his/her lawyer is prohibited, except when the judge has good reason to believe that those conversations constitute, themselves, the object or an element of a criminal offence.

The apprehension and any form of control of the correspondence between the defendant and his/her lawyer is prohibited, except when the judge has good reason to believe that those conversations constitute, themselves, the object or an element of a criminal offence [in such a case, however, as in the context of Article 187 (5) above, the execution of the measure is restricted to that specific offence, v.g., receiving stolen goods, and not to the offence that was being investigated, v.g., the theft from where the stolen goods proceed].

(1) The ministers of any religion, physicians, lawyers, journalists, members and employees of credit institutions and other people who have the right or duty to keep professional secrecy over certain facts may refuse to testify on facts covered by that right or duty.

(...)

(3) [However,] these persons can be obliged to testify, if a high court decides that, in the case, the relevance of the testimony overcomes the obligation to keep the secrecy, considering, among other, the indispensability of the testimony for ascertaining the truth of the facts, the gravity of the crime and the necessity to protect legal interests (...).

(4) The decision mentioned above is taken after consulting the entity that represents the profession at stake, in the terms and with the effects established in the legislation applicable to such an entity.

(5) Such an exception does not apply in any circumstances to religious secrecy.

(1) The persons mentioned in Articles 135 to 137 shall provide the judicial authority with the requested documents or objects which are in their possession and which ought to be seizes, save where they invoke, in writing, professional secrecy (...).

(2) In the case of professional secrecy (...), Article 135 (2) and (3) and Article 136 (2) apply accordingly.

(...)

Searches of offices of lawyers or physicians must, or otherwise it will be null, be personally presided over by a judge, who must previously communicate the measure to the president of the local council of the Bar Association or of the Association of Medical Doctors, respectively, in order for him/her or a delegate of his/hers to be present at its execution.

nationalActs.title: Regulamento das Condições de Detenção em Instalações da Polícia Judiciária e em Locais de Detenção Existentes nos Tribunais e em Serviços do Ministério Público (Despacho n.º 12786/2009, de 29 de maio))
nationalActs.titleEn: Regulation of the Detention Conditions in the Premises of the Judiciary Police and in Courts and Public Prosecution Services  (Dispatch no. 12786/2009, of 29 May)

provisions.textEn:
(1) An arrested person has the right to communicate, orally or in writing, at any time of the day or night, with his/her lawyer (...).

(...)

(3) The visit of the lawyer takes place in such a manner as to ensure that the conversation is not heard by any official.

(4) The content of the written texts or documents that the lawyer carries with him/her cannot be controlled or overseen.

provisions.comment: See also Articles 70 and 71 of the Code of Enforcement of Penalties and Measures involving Deprivation of Liberty (Law no. 115/2009, of 12 October), concerning the situation of inmates (viz., persons who have already been convicted and are serving a sentence of imprisonment).
provisions.textEn:
(1) [Upon his/her bringing into a prison facility,] The inmate has the right to make a phone call, free of charge, to a family member or a person of his/her trust, as well as to his/her lawyer.

(2) The phone call is overseen by the element of the surveillance and security services of the prison that brought the person into the prison facility, but the confidentiality of the conversation is guaranteed.

provisions.textEn: Communication with lawyers (...) is carried out in a reserved space which guarantees the confidentiality of the communication and its oversight, without a separating glass.

(1) The inmate has the right to communicate with his/her lawyer, personally and in a reserved manner, in a space which guarantees the confidentiality of the communication and its oversight.

(2) Communication with the lawyer is not dependent on authorisation.

(1) The inmate has the right to receive visits from his/her lawyer (...), during set periods (...) adequate to the solving of legal issues relating to him/her, without detriment to the possibility of receiving urgent visits.

(...)

(4) During the visit, only documents necessary for solving legal issues relating to the inmate can be exchanged with him/her, and their content cannot be controlled.

items.comment: Considering that in some cases Portuguese law admits the breach of professional secrecy by the lawyer of the defendant, it is not clear to us whether it fully complies with this provision of the Directive, which appears to admit no exceptions.

items.heading: Article 5
items.subHeading: The right to have a third person informed of the deprivation of liberty

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that suspects or accused persons who are deprived of liberty have the right to have at least one person, such as a relative or an employer, nominated by them, informed of their deprivation of liberty without undue delay if they so wish.

nationalActs.title: Regulamento das Condições de Detenção em Instalações da Polícia Judiciária e em Locais de Detenção Existentes nos Tribunais e em Serviços do Ministério Público (Despacho n.º 12786/2009, de 29 de maio))
nationalActs.titleEn: Regulation of the Detention Conditions in the Premises of the Judiciary Police and in Courts and Public Prosecution Services  (Dispatch no. 12786/2009, of 29 May)

provisions.textEn: Any person who is deprived of liberty must be informed immediately and in a comprehensible manner of the reasons of his/her arrest and of his/her rights, and he/she may exercise them as of the moment of his/her material arrest.
The arrested person has the right to inform immediately a family member or a person of his/her trust of his/her situation.

In order for the rights mentioned in the previous paragraphs to be exercised, the arrested person shall be provided the possibility to use the telephone of the service responsible for his/her detention, if a public telephone is unavailable.

nationalActs.title: Regulamento Geral dos Estabelecimentos Prisionais (Decreto-Lei n.º 51/2011, de 11 de Abril)

provisions.textEn:
(1) [Upon his/her bringing into a prison facility,] The inmate has the right to make a phone call, free of charge, to a family member or a person of his/her trust, as well as to his/her lawyer.

(2) The phone call is overseen by the element of the surveillance and security services of the prison that brought the person into the prison facility, but the confidentiality of the conversation is guaranteed.

provisions.textEn: The inmate is immediately informed of his/her rights and duties, duly explained and if necessary translated, and he/she is guaranteed the right to contact a family member or a person of his/her trust, as well as his/her lawyer.

items.text: 2. If the suspect or accused person is a child, Member States shall ensure that the holder of parental responsibility of the child is informed as soon as possible of the deprivation of liberty and of the reasons pertaining thereto, unless it would be contrary to the best interests of the child, in which case another appropriate adult shall be informed. For the purposes of this paragraph, a person below the age of 18 years shall be considered to be a child.

nationalActs.title: Código de Processo Penal (Decreto-Lei n.º 78/87, de 17 de Fevereiro)
nationalActs.titleEn: Code of Criminal Procedure (Decree-Law no. 78/87, of 17 February)

provisions.textEn: Without detriment to the continuation of the proceedings, the formal designation of a minor as a defendant is immediately communicated to the persons who hold parental responsibilities over him/her, to his/her legal representative, or to the person who holds his/her guardianship.

Unless otherwise provided for in the law, the defendant is specifically entitled, at all stages of the procedure, to the following rights: (...) if he/she is a minor (under 18 years old), to be accompanied in any procedural act that he/she is to attend by the persons who exercise parental responsibilities over him/her, by his/her legal representative or a person who holds his/her factual guardianship, or yet, if the former cannot be reached or special circumstances concerning his/her best interest so require, by another adequate person indicated by him/her and agreed to by the judicial authority.

If the minor did not indicate a different person to accompany him/her, or the person he/she indicated pursuant to paragraph (1) (i) above is not accepted by the judicial authority, this authority shall appoint, to that effect, a technician specialised for this type of assistance.

For the purposes of paragraphs (1) (i), (3) and (4) above, a person is presumed to be a minor if, after all due diligence has been carried out with a view to identifying the defendant, his/her age remains uncertain and there is reason to believe that he/she is a minor.

Assistance by an attorney is mandatory: (...) In any procedural act, save for the formal designation of the person as a defendant, whenever the person is blind, deaf, speechless, illiterate, unfamiliar with the Portuguese language, a person under 21 years old, ou the question has been raised whether he/she may be unimputable [owing to a mental disorder] or not completely imputable;

items.comment: In our view, this provision should be deemed as implemented, albeit in a somewhat indirect manner, based on provisions that will be explained further below in respect of Directive (EU) 2016/800, on procedural safeguards for juvenile defendants, namely Articles 58 (7), 61 (1), (d) and (i), (4) and (5) CCP. Note that a person below 18 years old is a minor under Portuguese law, so there is perfect harmony with the Directive.

items.text: 3. Member States may temporarily derogate from the application of the rights set out in paragraphs 1 and 2 where justified in the light of the particular circumstances of the case on the basis of one of the following compelling reasons:

items.subHeading: The right to communicate, while deprived of liberty, with third persons

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that suspects or accused persons who are deprived of liberty have the right to communicate without undue delay with at least one third person, such as a relative, nominated by them.

items.heading: Article 7
items.subHeading: The right to communicate with consular authorities

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that suspects or accused persons who are non-nationals and who are deprived of liberty have the right to have the consular authorities of their State of nationality informed of the deprivation of liberty without undue delay and to communicate with those authorities, if they so wish. However, where suspects or accused persons have two or more nationalities, they may choose which consular authorities, if any, are to be informed of the deprivation of liberty and with whom they wish to communicate.

nationalActs.title: Regulamento das Condições de Detenção em Instalações da Polícia Judiciária e em Locais de Detenção Existentes nos Tribunais e em Serviços do Ministério Público (Despacho n.º 12786/2009, de 29 de maio))
nationalActs.titleEn: Regulation of the Detention Conditions in the Premises of the Judiciary Police and in Courts and Public Prosecution Services  (Dispatch no. 12786/2009, of 29 May)

provisions.textEn: The information on the right to appoint a lawyer and to communicate with a family member, a person of one's trust, the embassy or the consulate, as well as the delievery of the booklet mentioned in the previous paragraph, shall be recorded in a document which should be signed by the concerned person. His/her refusal to sign shall also be recorded.
The information mentioned in the previous paragraph is provided to the arrested person in a language that he/she understands, and the presence of an interpreted is requested whenever it is necessary.
Foreign individuals who are arrested have the right to contact immediately the consular authorities of his country.

In order for the rights mentioned in the previous paragraphs to be exercised, the arrested person shall be provided the possibility to use the telephone of the service responsible for his/her detention, if a public telephone is unavailable.

nationalActs.title: Código da Execução das Penas e Medias Privativas da Liberdade  (Lei n.º 115/2009, de 12 de Outubro)
nationalActs.titleEn: Code of Enforcement of Penalties and Measures involving Deprivation of Liberty (Law no. 115/2009, of 12 October)

provisions.textEn: The enforcement of penalties and measures involving deprivation of liberty applied to inmates who are foreigners or belong to ethnic or linguistic minorities should, as much as possible, enable them to express their cultural values, to mitigate difficulties they might face in terms of social integration or command of the Portuguese language, namely by providing contact with consular or diplomatic authorities or organisations aimed at supporting immigrants, courses of Portuguese language, translation of documents or intervention of interpreters.

nationalActs.title: Regulamento Geral dos Estabelecimentos Prisionais (Decreto-Lei n.º 51/2011, de 11 de Abril)
nationalActs.titleEn: General Regulation of Prison Facilities (Decree-Law no. 51/2011, of 11 April)

provisions.textEn: Upon entry into the prison facility, the foreign or stateless inmate is informed of the possibility to give knowledge of his/her situation to the respective diplomatic or consular authority, or to the entity that represents his/her interests. A record is taken of what the inmate wishes be done.

Foreign or stateless inmates who have expressed their wish to contact the respective diplomatic or consular authority or the entity that represents their interests, are given the possibility to telephone that authority or entity free of charge, without detriment to the other telephone calls allowed for in Article 8.

When knowledge of the situation of the inmate has been given [to the authorities or entities mentioned in the previous Article], such authorities or entities are also given knowledge of the decisions and information concerning the inmate, without detriment to the other communications which are to be made base on other provisions of this legal instrument.

items.comment: There is no explicit provision in Portuguese law concerning the case where the person has two or more nationalities, but the following enable the person to choose which consular authorities are to be informed.

items.text: 2. Suspects or accused persons also have the right to be visited by their consular authorities, the right to converse and correspond with them and the right to have legal representation arranged for by their consular authorities, subject to the agreement of those authorities and the wishes of the suspects or accused persons concerned.

nationalActs.title: Regulamento das Condições de Detenção em Instalações da Polícia Judiciária e em Locais de Detenção Existentes nos Tribunais e em Serviços do Ministério Público (Despacho n.º 12786/2009, de 29 de maio))
nationalActs.titleEn: Regulation of the Detention Conditions in the Premises of the Judiciary Police and in Courts and Public Prosecution Services  (Dispatch no. 12786/2009, of 29 May)

provisions.comment: Nevertheless, this legal instrument should feature a provision explicitly providing for the right to be visited by consular authorities.
provisions.textEn: Foreign individuals who are arrested have the right to contact immediately the consular authorities of his country.

nationalActs.title: Regulamento Geral dos Estabelecimentos Prisionais (Decreto-Lei n.º 51/2011, de 11 de Abril)
nationalActs.titleEn: General Regulation of Prison Facilities (Decree-Law no. 51/2011, of 11 April)

provisions.textEn: Communication with (...) diplomatic or consular authorities in the exercise of their functions is carried out in a reserved space which guarantees the confidentiality of the communication and its oversight, without a separating glass.

(1) The visits of diplomatic or consular authorities are not dependent on authorisation and they take place in business days, during the timeframe set by the director of the prison facility, within its normal working hours.

(2) An authority wishing to visit the inmate shall inform the director of the prison facility 24 hours beforehand, in order to obtain the consent of the inmate to being visited.

(3) Articles 102 to 104, on communication between the inmate and his/her lawyer, apply with the necessary adaptations.

items.comment:
Only partially implemented.

Despite the provisions mentioned below, there is no provision in the Regulation of the Detention Conditions in the Premises of the Judiciary Police and in Courts and Public Prosecution Services explicitly and specifically establishing that suspects or accused persons who are arrested have the right to be visited by their consular authorities, the right to converse and correspond with them. And such a provision would, in our view, be necessary to ensure full implementation. As for the right to have legal representation arranged for by consular authorities, no such provision exists either, but such a right is in our view possible to draw from other provisions, namely from the general right of defendants to appoint a lawyer of their choice.

items.text: 3. The exercise of the rights laid down in this Article may be regulated by national law or procedures, provided that such law or procedures enable full effect to be given to the purposes for which these rights are intended.

items.heading: Article 8
items.subHeading: General conditions for applying temporary derogations
items.comment: Regarding the issue of temporary derogation of rights regulated in the Directive, namely in Article 3 (3) (a), Article 5 (3) and (4), and Article 8, the problem lies in Article 143 (4) CCP, which provides that “[i]n cases of terrorism and violent or highly organised criminality, public prosecution may order that the arrested person, prior to his/her first judicial interrogation, does not communicate with anyone, except for his/her lawyer”. This provision requires no further condition than the fact that the case concerns terrorism or violent / highly organised criminality. A Report by the Commission of the Portuguese Parliament on Constitutional Issues, Rights and Guarantees, concerning the proposal that would eventually result in the Directive 2013/48/UE, remarks that the provision of the Directive may be seen as “excessive”, considering that “the special gravity of such cases and the complexity of their investigation may justify a restriction of the rights of the arrested person”. Be that as it may, the fact is that Portuguese law does not, at present, comply with the Directive on this particular point.

Temporary derogations under Article 3(5) or (6) may be authorised only by a duly reasoned decision taken on a case-by-case basis, either by a judicial authority, or by another competent authority on condition that the decision can be submitted to judicial review. The duly reasoned decision shall be recorded using the recording procedure in accordance with the law of the Member State concerned.

3. Temporary derogations under Article 5(3) may be authorised only on a case-by-case basis, either by a judicial authority, or by another competent authority on condition that the decision can be submitted to judicial review.

items.heading: Article 9
items.comment:
Only partially implemented, and only to a narrow extent.

Portuguese law does not really contain any rules aimed at regulating the case in which the defendant does not intend to exercise his/her right to a lawyer. It is clear to us that national legislation should be adopted to accommodate this provision of the Directive. As acknowledged before, Portuguese law does confer on the defendant a wide right to assistance by a lawyer, several provisions aimed at promoting the exercise of such a right, and even cases where such an assistance is mandatory irrespective of the defendant’s will (which incidentally is why in Portuguese criminal procedure the defence attorney is conceived of as an actual procedural subject, rather than a mere projection of the defendant). However, by regulating in detail the waiver of this right the Directive reinforces it even further, in a way that is qualitatively different from any of the ways in which Portuguese law protects such a right. This leads us to the conclusion that Article 9 of the Directive currently lacks implementation in Portuguese law.

items.text: 2. The waiver, which can be made in writing or orally, shall be noted, as well as the circumstances under which the waiver was given, using the recording procedure in accordance with the law of the Member State concerned.

items.heading: Article 10
items.subHeading: The right of access to a lawyer in European arrest warrant proceedings
items.comment: Only partially implemented. Problems concern Article 10 (4) and (5).

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that a requested person has the right of access to a lawyer in the executing Member State upon arrest pursuant to the European arrest warrant.

nationalActs.title: Regime Jurídico do Mandado de Detenção Europeu (Lei n.º 65/2003, de 23 de Agosto)
nationalActs.titleEn: Law on the European Arrest Warrant (Law no. 65/2003, of 23 August)

provisions.textEn: The person arrested [pursuant to an EAW] has the right to be assisted by a lawyer.

items.text: 2. With regard to the content of the right of access to a lawyer in the executing Member State, requested persons shall have the following rights in that Member State:

(a)

the right of access to a lawyer in such time and in such a manner as to allow the requested persons to exercise their rights effectively and in any event without undue delay from deprivation of liberty;

provisions.comment: See the respective provisions above.
provisions.textEn: The arrest of a person [pursuant to an EAW] abides by the same requirements provided for in the CCP for the arrest of suspects.

provisions.comment: See the relevant provisions of the CCP, above.
provisions.textEn: Articles 57 to 67 of the CCP [on the formal designation of a person as a defendant (arguido), the rights and duties springing from this status, etc.] apply as appropriate, and the person sought on account of a EAW, when arrested, should be provided with a document informing him/her of the rights mentioned in the previous paragraphs.
The Code of Criminal Procedure applies in a subsidiary manner to the procedure of execution of an EAW.

items.text:
(b)

the right to meet and communicate with the lawyer representing them;

(c)

the right for their lawyer to be present and, in accordance with procedures in national law, participate during a hearing of a requested person by the executing judicial authority. Where a lawyer participates during the hearing this shall be noted using the recording procedure in accordance with the law of the Member State concerned.

provisions.textEn: Before hearing the person sought pursuant to an EAW, the judge appoints a lawyer to him/her, if he/she has not yet appointed one.

The consent mentioned in item (b) of the previous paragraph [sc., the consent to being re-surrendered to another Member State following the execution of an EAW] must: (...) Be provided with the assistance of a lawyer.

(1) If the sought person does not consent to being surrendered to the issuing Member State, the floor is given to his/her lawyer, so that he/she may present the opposition to the surrender.

(...)

(5) After the production of evidence, the floor is given to the public prosecution and the lawyer of the concerned person, so that they may adduce oral allegations.
If Portugal is the issuing Member State, the waiver [to the specialty rule] mentioned in paragraph (2) (f) of this provision must: (...) Be provided with the assistance of a lawyer.

items.comment: Regarding the recording procedure, see again the provisions of the CCP that regulate this issue. Such provisions apply ex vi Article 34 LEAW, transcribed above.

items.text: 3. The rights provided for in Articles 4, 5, 6, 7, 9, and, where a temporary derogation under Article 5(3) is applied, in Article 8, shall apply, mutatis mutandis, to European arrest warrant proceedings in the executing Member State.
items.comment: See the provisions and comments attached to Article 10 (2) (b) of this Directive, which confer on persons sought pursuant to an EAW the same rights and duties that are conferred on defendants in criminal proceedings.

items.text: 4. The competent authority in the executing Member State shall, without undue delay after deprivation of liberty, inform requested persons that they have the right to appoint a lawyer in the issuing Member State. The role of that lawyer in the issuing Member State is to assist the lawyer in the executing Member State by providing that lawyer with information and advice with a view to the effective exercise of the rights of requested persons under Framework Decision 2002/584/JHA.
items.comment: This provision may, at best, be deemed as partially implemented, for there is no explicit provision imposing on Portuguese authorities, as executing authorities, a duty to, without undue delay after deprivation of liberty, inform requested persons that they have the right to appoint a lawyer in the issuing Member State. This might be achieved with an extensive interpretation of Article 61 (1) (e) and (h) CCP, applicable to EAW proceedings ex vi Articles 17 (4) and 34 LEAW (transcribed above), but this is by no means clear. If a lawyer does come to be appointed in the issuing Member State, then his/her role will naturally include assistance, information and advice to the lawyer in the executing Member State, but there is no explicit provision on this either.

items.text: 5. Where requested persons wish to exercise the right to appoint a lawyer in the issuing Member State and do not already have such a lawyer, the competent authority in the executing Member State shall promptly inform the competent authority in the issuing Member State. The competent authority of that Member State shall, without undue delay, provide the requested persons with information to facilitate them in appointing a lawyer there.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.text: 6. The right of a requested person to appoint a lawyer in the issuing Member State is without prejudice to the time-limits set out in Framework Decision 2002/584/JHA or the obligation on the executing judicial authority to decide, within those time-limits and the conditions defined under that Framework Decision, whether the person is to be surrendered.

items.heading: Article 12

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings, as well as requested persons in European arrest warrant proceedings, have an effective remedy under national law in the event of a breach of the rights under this Directive.
items.comment: The provisions and comments attached to 10 of Directive 2016/343 on presumption of innocence apply squarely here.

items.text: 2. Without prejudice to national rules and systems on the admissibility of evidence, Member States shall ensure that, in criminal proceedings, in the assessment of statements made by suspects or accused persons or of evidence obtained in breach of their right to a lawyer or in cases where a derogation to this right was authorised in accordance with Article 3(6), the rights of the defence and the fairness of the proceedings are respected.
items.comment: In our view, the provisions indicated throughout this implementation assessment, notably those mentioned with reference to Article 4 of the Directive, as well as those mentioned throughout the Directive on presumption of innocence, suffice to ensure that the rights of the defence and the fairness of the proceedings are respected.
